meta.embargo_rationale: 252 trading days = the slowest signal-component horizon used ANYWHERE in the base construction or its overlays: the 12-month (252-trading-day) total-return rule (research/cta/_s1_ensemble_93name.py) and the 10-month SMA rule (~210 trading days, Meb Faber convention, same file) are the two slowest axes; Axis-C causal_hmm_regime_posterior's min_train=252 (ctaB_pipeline.py) independently corroborates the same 252-day figure. All other components (vol_window=20, ewma_0.94 ~15.7d memory, corr_window<=120, the GZ-style drawdown-brake's own m_t which looks back only to running-peak-to-date with no extra fixed window) are faster/shorter. 252 (>=210) is therefore used, matching ctaB_pipeline.py's own EMBARGO_TRADING_DAYS constant exactly -- not re-derived independently, reused because it is the SAME base construction's own frozen figure.

cpcv.drop_reason: a (group,group) combo is dropped by cpcv_paths() itself when, after removing the +/-252-day embargo halo around each of the k=2 test groups, the remaining test segment has <=20 obs or zero variance -- with n_obs=2046 split into 8 groups of ~256 obs each, a 252-day embargo on EACH side of EACH of the 2 test groups consumes very close to an entire adjacent group's width, so most combinations that include two adjacent (or once-removed) groups collapse to a near-empty or empty remaining test segment and are dropped; only combinations of groups that are far enough apart (and/or near the sample edges, where there is no embargo on the outward side) survive with >20 obs remaining.

dsr_informational.waterfall_stopping_points_rationale: The combined policy was reached via a MECHANICAL waterfall (Step A -> C -> D-corr -> D-index), not a fitted grid search: at each step there was exactly one pre-specified next overlay to test and the waterfall stops (or proceeds) based on a pre-registered pass/fail gate, not on picking the best of many. That gives AT MOST 4 distinct configurations that could ever actually have been the 'final' one the waterfall stopped at (stop-after-A, stop-after-C, stop-after-D-corr, stop-after-D-index) -- not 2^5=32 (all combinations of 5 independent overlays a grid search would have implied), and not even 2^4=16 restricted to the 4 steps actually walked, because the waterfall's sequential accept/reject logic collapses the combinatorial overlay space down to a single ordered path with one decision (continue Y/N) per step, i.e. a linear chain of <=4 stopping points rather than a tree/lattice of configurations.
dsr_informational.contrast_note: At N_trials=2 (near-naive lower-bound reference; N_trials=1 is degenerate for this PPF-based DSR formula) vs N_trials=4 (honest waterfall count) vs N_trials=32 (what a full independent grid search over all 5 overlays' on/off combinations would have implied, ignoring within-overlay parameter variation which would push the true grid count higher still) -- the DSR haircut from 2->4 is small precisely because the waterfall's sequential, pre-registered, gate-based structure never actually multiplicity-tested a combinatorial lattice of overlay on/off states; it tested a short ordered chain. This is DSR/PBO reported INFORMATIONALLY ONLY per the frozen adoption-gate convention (ctaB_pipeline.py docstring: 'DSR/PBO are computed and reported INFORMATIONALLY ONLY -- they never gate adoption here') -- neither DSR nor PBO is a pass/fail gate for this program.
